newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea resume missing-in-action talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea resume missing-in-action talks.

text.p: North Korea and the United States resumed talks on Sunday on possible joint efforts to account for the 8,100 or so Americans still listed as missing from the 1950-53 Korean War.
The U.S. Defence Department said the discussions were taking place at an undisclosed location in New York and were expected to last through at least Thursday.

The U.S.-North Korean missing-in-action talks were last held in May 1996. They were derailed when a North Korean submarine packed with commandos that aground off the South Korean coast last September.
The new round of talks will also deal with U.S. questions about "alleged" Americans possibly living in North Korea, Lt. Colonel Joan Ferguson, a Pentagon spokeswoman, said.
She said other topics included a schedule for resuming joint excavations at sites believed to contain remains of U.S. servicemen buried or shot down during the war.
An initial excavation last year yielded the remains of one U.S. serviceman which were returned to his family last July.

The talks are separate from negotiations that broke off last month in New York in which the United States and South Korea urged Pyongyang to begin four-way peace talks with China to negotiate a formal end to the 1950-53 war.
